questions.question: Which structure surrounds every living cell and regulates exchange with its surroundings?
Which structure assembles proteins in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
Where is most of a typical animal cell's DNA located?
Which organelle carries out photosynthesis in plant cells?
Which structure provides extra support outside the plasma membrane of a plant cell?
What is the cytoplasm?
choices: The cell's contents outside the nucleus, enclosed by the plasma membrane
The rigid covering outside a plant cell
The fluid outside all cells in a tissue

questions.question: Which organelle modifies and sorts many proteins for transport?
What distinguishes a prokaryotic cell from a eukaryotic cell?
choices: A prokaryotic cell has no plasma membrane
A prokaryotic cell cannot contain DNA
A prokaryotic cell has no ribosomes
A prokaryotic cell lacks a membrane-bound nucleus

questions.question: Why do cells need selectively permeable membranes?
choices: To make all internal concentrations match the surroundings
To prevent any material from ever entering
To regulate entry and exit while maintaining internal conditions
To replace the need for chemical reactions

questions.question: Why are mitochondria important in many eukaryotic cells?
choices: They help produce ATP during aerobic cellular respiration
They store the cell's only copy of genetic information
They create the cell wall from mineral crystals
They sort all proteins for export from the cell

questions.question: How does a large central vacuole help many plant cells?
choices: It assembles every protein used by the cell
It replaces the chloroplast during photosynthesis
It directs chromosome separation during mitosis
It stores water and helps maintain pressure against the cell wall

questions.question: What is a key statement of cell theory?
choices: Only animals are composed of cells
Living organisms consist of cells, and cells arise from existing cells
Cells arise mainly from nonliving minerals
All cells have identical shapes and organelles

questions.question: Why can different cells in one organism have different shapes?
choices: Each cell must belong to a different species
Their structures are specialized for different functions
Their shapes are unrelated to their activities
Only cells without DNA can change shape

questions.question: How does the rough endoplasmic reticulum differ from the smooth endoplasmic reticulum?
choices: Smooth ER contains the cell's chromosomes
Rough ER has ribosomes attached to its surface

questions.question: Why are many cells small rather than extremely large?
choices: Smaller size often improves exchange relative to cell volume
Small cells avoid the need for membranes
Large cells cannot contain genetic information
Small cells do not require nutrients

questions.question: A gland cell exports large amounts of protein. Which structures would be particularly important?
choices: Ribosomes, rough ER, and Golgi apparatus

questions.question: A cell has DNA, ribosomes, and a plasma membrane but no nucleus. Which classification fits?
A plant cell loses much of its stored water and becomes less firm. Which structure is most directly involved?
A microscope shows many similar cells working together to contract. What level of organization is being observed?
Two cells have similar volume, but one has a highly folded membrane. What advantage can the folds provide?
choices: More surface area for exchange or membrane processes
Less need for any cellular energy
